title: Rigorous MITM Bounds for Fixed S-Boxes
summary: The stated S-box property holds on average for random S-boxes but not for fixed ones, leaving rigorous MITM list-size and attack-complexity bounds unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Establish rigorous list-size and attack-complexity bounds for the MITM model with concrete fixed S-boxes, replacing the global heuristic on which the current complexity estimates rely. Specifically, for a $w$-bit cell and fixed edges of combined width $u \leq 1$, either prove conditions ensuring that the cell has exactly $2^{w(1-u)}$ admissible values or derive rigorous alternative bounds sufficient to justify the resulting attack complexity. The result must apply to fixed S-boxes, not merely hold on average when S-boxes are drawn at random.

scope.domain: Meet-in-the-middle cryptanalysis of concrete permutations modeled with fixed S-boxes.
assumptions: The fixed edges have combined width $u \leq 1$.
The current list-size assignment of $2^{w(1-u)}$ admissible values is heuristic for fixed S-boxes.
parameters: $u$: combined width of the fixed edges
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove conditions yielding the stated exact admissible-value count for fixed S-boxes, or establish rigorous alternative bounds that justify the resulting MITM attack complexity.

citations.label: Simplified MITM Modeling for Permutations: New (Quantum) Attacks

progress.summary: The source introduces a simplifying S-box assumption that would hold on average for randomly drawn S-boxes but not for fixed S-boxes. It states that the final complexity estimates instead rely on a global heuristic.
citation_labels: André Schrottenloher et al., Simplified MITM Modeling for Permutations: New (Quantum) Attacks
